subject.title: [Feature]: 内置健壮性机制：Watchdog、全局错误处理、自动恢复

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in Gateway watchdog and recovery ladder, and which recovery actions should be default versus opt-in?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses startup, repair, config migration, restart control, notifications, and security-sensitive operator authority, so code inspection alone cannot choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Keep as design umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical umbrella while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

options.title: Split to narrower issues
options.body: Replace this broad issue with separate tracked work for crash-loop suppression, degraded startup, doctor repair, health schema, and user notification policy.

options.title: Reject core ownership
options.body: Close this as out of core scope and document plugin, supervisor, or operator-owned recovery patterns instead.

recommendation.title: Keep as design umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical umbrella while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway restart protection and fatal-error handling history makes this the best available routing owner for the product boundary decision.
